key_findings.value: M2-HQ optical micrograph (500 µm scale bar) shows a lighter matrix with scattered dark features.

purpose.value: Microstructural imaging of the homogenized + water-quenched M2 (M2-HQ) sample

source.reason: Fig. 3 provides the M2-HQ micrograph; b0024 states that an optical microscope (OM) and SEM were used to obtain microstructural images of the different samples.

boundary_and_initial_conditions.value: Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C (M2) composition; equilibrium phases predicted as a function of temperature; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; 1 % Si addition to the 3Al system introduces δ-ferrite in the intercritical temperature range (ICT band ~600-1000 °C).

source.reason: b0021 and Figs. 1f/2 describe Thermo-Calc (TCFE9) equilibrium phase-fraction and austenite-composition predictions for the Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C (M2) alloy composition, to which M2-HQ belongs.

processing_steps_notes.value: The two steel compositions (M1 = Fe-8Mn-3Al-0.2C and M2 = Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C) were fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of raw materials throughout the ingot.

source.reason: b0023 describes fabrication of the two steels (including M2, the 3Al-1Si alloy) by vacuum arc melting with 4× remelting.
b0023/Table 1 state the homogenization is followed by water quenching, which defines M2-HQ.
b0023 and Table 1 (b0037) give a homogenization duration of 2 h.

processing_steps_notes.value: Homogenization of as-cast samples was carried out at 1100 °C for 2 h, followed by water quenching. This homogenized + water-quenched condition is designated M2-HQ (Nomenclature for 3Al-1Si (M2)).

source.reason: b0023 and Table 1 (b0037) list 'Homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching)' as the M2-HQ condition.
b0023 and Table 1 (b0037) give the homogenization temperature as 1100 °C for the M2-HQ condition.
Microstructure corresponds to the homogenization + water-quenching step (sequence 2).
Micrograph of the water-quenched M2 (M2-HQ) sample is shown in the processing schematic of Fig. 3; no quantitative phase analysis is reported for the HQ condition.
Fig. 3 shows the micrograph for the water-quenched M2 (M2-HQ) condition described as a lighter matrix with scattered dark features.

overall_structure.value: Homogenized + water-quenched M2 microstructure: the optical micrograph (500 µm scale bar) shows a lighter matrix with scattered dark features.

source.reason: Structural information for the M2-HQ condition is limited to the micrograph inset in the Fig. 3 processing schematic.

unmapped_findings: δ-ferrite in M2 steel is stated to form while soaking at 1100 °C before hot rolling (physically the same temperature as the 1100 °C homogenization), and some fraction of α-ferrite forms from γ at finish-rolling temperatures (~900 °C); however, the paper does not explicitly assign δ-ferrite to the M2-HQ (homogenized + water-quenched) state.

No tensile, hardness, or quantitative phase-fraction (XRD/EBSD) measurement is reported specifically for the M2-HQ condition; the mechanical properties and quantitative phase analysis in this paper refer only to the M2-HR (hot-rolled) and M2-IA (intercritically annealed) conditions.
